tells.plain: Indigo-to-violet gradients on a hero or button: the colour of countless generated landing pages.
tells.technical: Flagged as any gradient fill (gradient, gradient-src) and as indigo or violet palettes (palette-purple, purple-src). A neutral scrim over a photo is the one allowed gradient.

tells.plain: Headline words filled with a colour gradient so they glow.
tells.technical: Text clipped to a gradient background. Flat ink carries the message; the effect adds no information and costs contrast.

tells.plain: Emoji standing in for icons or bullets: rockets, sparkles and checkmarks in headings.
tells.technical: Emoji codepoints in visible text or source. Emoji render differently per platform and cannot be themed; use words or a real icon set.

tells.plain: Frosted translucent cards stacked over blurred backgrounds.
tells.technical: More than one backdrop-filter blur surface on a marketing page, or any in an app. One blurred sticky bar is tolerable.

tells.plain: Every card lifted by a soft shadow, so nothing sits on the page.
tells.technical: At-rest box-shadows on marketing pages and heavy panel shadows in apps. Separate surfaces by a tone step or space; keep shadows for things that really float.

tells.plain: A card with one thick coloured stripe down its left edge.
tells.technical: A border of 3 px or more on a single side, with the others thin or absent. Reads as a generated callout; use a tint or an icon.

tells.plain: A card sitting inside another card, each with its own border and padding.
tells.technical: A container with card styling (background, radius, border or shadow) nested inside another. Flatten the inner one with spacing, type or a tone change.

tells.plain: Three or four identical cards, each topped with a small icon, a title and two lines.
tells.technical: A row of structurally identical siblings each led by a small icon, plus icon chips and tiles. Replace with one composed section built around a single idea.

tells.plain: A tiny uppercase label above every heading ("FEATURES", "HOW IT WORKS").
tells.technical: Short, small, letter-spaced text immediately above a heading, rendered or in source. One per page is a choice; one per section is a template.

tells.plain: The same handful of fonts used by every generated page, or a font that failed to load.
tells.technical: Source scan of a fixed list of overused families (default-font-src) plus a render check that a declared font is not rendering as its fallback.

tells.plain: Lorem ipsum, "John Doe", round numbers and "Your text here" left in the page.
tells.technical: Lorem text, stock placeholder names and obviously fake data in source and on screen. Believable, internally consistent data is part of the design.

tells.plain: Decorative 01 / 02 / 03 numbers before headings.
tells.technical: Zero-padded or index-style numerals used as ornament rather than as a real sequence.

tells.plain: Body text justified into uneven word gaps and rivers.
tells.technical: text-align: justify on a block with 80 or more characters of its own text. Left-aligned ragged-right text reads better on the web.

tells.plain: Heading levels jump from h1 to h4 to pick a size.
tells.technical: A heading whose level is more than one deeper than the previous. Headings are structure for assistive tech; size comes from CSS.

tells.plain: Body copy in pale grey that looks elegant and is hard to read.
tells.technical: Text below the WCAG floor (contrast) or a soft grey body under 7:1 (grey-body); declared token pairs that miss 4.5:1 (token-contrast).

tells.plain: The warm cream, terracotta and charcoal palette that signals "an AI wrote this".
tells.technical: Palette families matched in rendered colours (palette-cream, palette-terracotta, palette-claude) and in source (claude-palette-src).

tells.plain: Sentences held together with em dashes.
tells.technical: More than four em dashes across the source files (em-dash-src, WARN only). One or two is style; a habit is a voice that is not yours.

tells.plain: Every box and divider drawn with a thin grey line.
tells.technical: Counts of 1 px borders and divider rules, and even 1 px outlines on boxes. Use fill steps and space to separate.

tells.plain: Animations that keep running when the system asks for less motion.
tells.technical: The capture matrix reruns with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and fails any element still moving over 10 ms.

tells.plain: transition: all, looping bounce or pulse classes and ease-in used on everything.
tells.technical: Source patterns: transition: all (animates every property), Tailwind animate-bounce, animate-ping and animate-pulse classes, and the ease-in keyword (ease-in-out is allowed).

tells.plain: A headline that could belong to any product: "Build faster. Ship better."
tells.technical: The reviewer asks the competitor test: swap in a rival's name; if the headline still works, it says nothing. No rule can judge meaning.

tells.plain: Three equal columns of feature, benefit and detail, with no order of importance.
tells.technical: Judged from the screenshot: three siblings of equal size, weight and copy length. Distinct from icon-card-grid, which is mechanically detectable.

tells.plain: Smiling people at laptops or handshakes in place of the real product.
tells.technical: Judged from images: generic stock photography instead of product screens, artefacts or specific people.

tells.plain: Shapes, blobs, grids and glows that point at nothing.
tells.technical: The reviewer asks of each decorative element what it explains or whom it helps. If neither, cut it.

tells.plain: Nothing on the page could not appear on any competitor's site.
tells.technical: Fails the idea gate: no one live thing that is specific to this product, and no choice a competitor would not make.

tells.plain: Gaps between sections and elements drift with no shared scale.
tells.technical: Judged from screenshots and the spacing tokens: paddings and margins off the spacing scale, or inconsistent between like parts.

tells.plain: Every block competes with the same size, weight and colour.
tells.technical: Judged from the first-screen screenshot: no single focal point and more than one competing accent.

tells.plain: Round, impressive statistics ("10x faster", "99.9%") with no source.
tells.technical: Judged from copy: figures presented as proof without a measurement, date or source.
